x-note: PRD §25.15 security regression inputs. Every entry names the threat it exercises and the invariant that must hold. The invariant is the point: a fixture without an assertion is just an odd repository, and a future reader needs to know what failure looks like.

cases.description: Project instructions and a patch that both reference ../ outside the workspace.
cases.invariant: Every read and write resolves inside the canonical workspace root, or fails with PATH_OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE. §14.2, AC-11.
cases.notes: The normalizer deliberately preserves '..' rather than collapsing it, so the approval card shows the traversal attempt and the Rust guard is the component that rejects it.

cases.description: A symlink inside the workspace pointing at an absolute path outside it.
cases.invariant: A symlink whose target leaves the workspace is refused even though the link itself is inside. §14.2 step 6, AC-12.
cases.setup: The link is created by the test rather than committed, because git does not preserve a link to an absolute host path portably.

cases.description: File content carrying CSI, OSC, and DCS sequences plus a bare ESC.
cases.invariant: Nothing reaching the screen can move the cursor, set the window title, write the clipboard, or start a hyperlink that was not allowlisted. §6.20, AC-33.
cases.expectedBehaviour: sanitizeText strips the sequences; the surrounding text survives.

cases.description: AGENTS.md and a Skill body that instruct the agent to exfiltrate credentials and ignore its policy.
cases.invariant: Untrusted text is wrapped as data (§11.4's wrapUntrusted) and cannot grant a permission. Nothing the model reads reaches `allow`. §24.1 invariant 1.
cases.expectedBehaviour: The injected instructions appear in the prompt inside an untrusted wrapper, and any action they request still requires approval.

cases.description: Files containing credential-shaped strings, and a patch that would write one.
cases.invariant: A credential-shaped literal is redacted in output and refused on write unless explicitly approved. §9.8, §12.6, AC-39.
cases.notes: The values here are syntactically plausible but are not real credentials; they are constructed to trip the detector.

cases.description: A file with a single very long line and a very large line count.
cases.invariant: Inline output is capped and the remainder becomes an artifact; the context is never flooded. §11.6, §18.17, AC-44.
cases.expectedBehaviour: The observation is truncated with an artifact reference and a stated omission count.
